articleTitle: Recent Progress in Development of Multiband Feed Horns (Review)
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This paper proposes overview of the multiband feed system for reflector-type antennas. Coaxial, multimode Potter's type structures, multiband corrugated and dielectric loaded feed horns is discussed below.

articleTitle: 60 years of electrically small antennas theory
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In 2007 60 years from the moment of the publication of the first theoretical work which have proved fundamental limits of achievable parameter!, so-called Electrically Small Antennas (ESA) are executed. On the eve of a anniversary of the given event -it is high time to sum up the 60-years way gone by theorists and developers of aerials in understanding of limiting restrictions in realization effective of ESA-solutions. The given report also is devoted to this review.

articleTitle: EBG resonator antennas: State of the art and prospects
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This article presents the recent developments on Electromagnetic Band Gap (EBG) resonator antennas. After reminding the working principles of such radiating devices, a state of the art is presented to show main applications of these antennas in cluding high directivity solutions, multiband devices, omnidirectionnal coverages, focal feeds for reflector and tuning. Finally, some prospects are given for future im provements.

articleTitle: Low cost signal source for multi-band multi-mode wireless systems
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In multi-band multi-mode radio architectures, a number of local oscillator (LO) frequencies are required in order to process the information in various frequency bands. Since oscillators consume a substantial part of the chip area and battery power, this article describes the design approach of RCO (reconfigurable concurrent oscillator) that simultaneously generates generate multiple frequencies with the user having an option of choosing a frequency or combination of them that eliminate the need of lossy switches for switching the frequency band, thereby improves the throughput.

articleTitle: Beauty of fractals design of fractal antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In this paper, beauty of fractals, some bases of its, processes, parameters and pictures of Mandelbrot and Julia sets are represented. Algorithms of computer-aided design of the dipole and planar fractal antennas of different orders are described. Current distribution, characteristics of impedance, distribution of near electromagnetic field and radiation of the fractal antennas are analyzed. Represented antennas structures may be used in modern radiocommunication systems.

articleTitle: Antenna array signal processing with high-resolution by modified beamspace music algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of determining the directions-of-arrival (DOA's) of narrow-band emitter signals impinging on an antenna array. A modified beamspace MUSIC algorithm for high-resolution array processing is presented. Simulation results are included to show the improved performance of proposed estimator at threshold signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband tapered-slot antenna with non-uniform resistive loading
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Several designs of tapered-slot antennas for ultra-wideband applications such as ground penetrating radar are described. The antennas for subsurface imaging must be damped to decrease clutter arising from the ringing of the antenna. The ringing is caused by the internal or open-end reflections as well as multiple reflections between the antenna and ground surface. In the proposed design, the ringing has been partially suppressed by corrugations and/or resistive films applied on the antenna flares in different ways. Performance of the antennas has been estimated using the electromagnetic simulation software. It was found that resistive loading of the antenna flares results in decrease of the return loss and increase of the directivity at low frequencies that diminishes the clutter. This is demonstrated also in the simulations by the impulse waveform received by a small probe placed in the antenna near field.

articleTitle: A Dualband Coaxial Dielectric-loaded Feed horn
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A novel dualband hybrid-mode coaxial feed horn partially loaded by dielectric is proposed. It has a simple structure and demonstrates good electrical performance over wide frequency range within each operating frequency band, when separation between operating bands is 3:1 or more.

articleTitle: Matrix theory of dissipative antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A theory of a phased antenna array with lossy radiating elements is elaborated. The theory is based on representation of a radiating system as the equivalent multi-port linking amplitudes of traveling waves in transmission lines with amplitudes of spherical waves in free space. Relations for calculation of blocks of a scattering matrix, that defines parameters of this multiport, are obtained under assumption that initial parameters of the radiating system the impedance matrix and partial radiation patterns (RP) - are known. A procedure for calculation of these parameters is described. It is based on the solution, with the moments method, of the electromagnetic boundary problem of the antenna array excitation at the alternating excitation of its inputs. The given relations allow effectively calculating parameters of transmitting and receiving phased antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Design of Wire Antennas with using of Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Methods of computer-aided design and an optimization of antennas with a using of genetic algorithms are represented in the paper. A general basis of the design and the optimization of antennas are discussed. Main ideas, parameters, structure and network properties of the genetic algorithms are described. Results of the design antennas are presented.

articleTitle: Contour optimization of a planar broadband dipole using genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The application of genetic algorithm (GA) optimization to the design and analysis for planar broadband dipoles of bow-tie type is presented. Primary attention is given to the analysis of the radiating contour profile of the bow-tie antenna. The planar dipole antenna is proposed for UWB communications in the frequency range 3.1-10.6 GHz. A printed design of the proposed antenna is defined for return loss < -10 dB and antenna gain > 2 dB over the whole frequency range.

articleTitle: Effects of the element separation on the noise performance of receiving antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Antenna arrays of closely separated elements can be used to achieve a large field of view of a radio telescope with highly efficient multiple beams. However, due to strong mutual coupling effects which exist in such dense arrays, the receiver noise can degrade. To reduce this noise degradation, the optimal noise match condition should be satisfied for all scan angles. This paper presents results of the noise performance analysis of small arrays of dipoles that were obtained for several element separation distances covering both conventional and dense arrays. The receiver noise temperatures are calculated for different noise match situations and the minimum noise temperature conditions are discussed.

articleTitle: Diffraction field of the vertical dipole from sphere with aperture, screening by the dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The application of the regularization task of the radiation field by a screening sphere with the circular aperture is proposed. We examine the radiation field of the vertical electrical dipole from sphere. We solve auxiliary integral equations of Abel's type and select main part of functional equations by introducing the small parameter. We obtain linear algebraic equations of second kind of Fredholm's type. New possibilities of improvement of computational algorithms and different characteristics of spherical antenna are discussed.

Author Keywords: method of regularization characteristics of spherical screening antenna

articleTitle: Drosophila melanogaster viability and mutability under the influence of low energy microwave monochromatic and ultra wideband impulse field
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The influence of microwave radiation (int = 35 GHz, intensity P = 30, 70, 180, 265 mW /cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and ultra wideband irradiation at irradiation intensity of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>, 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>, 10 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> on stocks of Drosophila melanogaster was investigated. Irradiation was performed on the stage of egg< exposure time was 10 sec... Irradiation by monochromatic radiation (35 GHz) of intensity 70, 180 and 265 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> negatively influences upon the viability of Drosophila. No viability decrease registered after ultra wideband irradiation. Monochromatic microwave radiation induced dominant lethal mutations (DLM). The effect of radiation depends on state of polarizations of radiation. Linear polarized radiation and right circular polarized radiation induce more DLM than left circular polarized radiation. Ultra wideband .impulse radiation induced no significant decrease of Drosophila viability. Incidence of DLM increased after ultra wideband impulse irradiation at the intensity 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Diffraction radiation antennas for SHF and EHF radiosystems
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Diffraction radiation antennas are described, consisting of a dielectric waveguide and a diffraction grating. A wide variety of antennas models are presented, a number of them have been used in SHF and EHF radiosystems. Among them: antenna for 8 mm satellite radiometer, linear antennas for airborne side looking radars, antennas with cosecant-type radiation pattern, planar and linear scanning antennas meant for automobile radars, etc. New opportunities in antenna design are discussed in connection with technology and simulation progress.

articleTitle: Laser interferometer antenna array records seismo-acoustic earth strains
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The recent results of the design and application of laser interferometer array for recording the seismic and acoustic strains of the earth ground are presented. The system contains the number of precise laser interferometers with the space distanced measuring arms. Interferometer gauges with the base length from 5 m up to 300 m have been used. The design and operation of constituent laser interferometer units, data exquisition system, and preliminary results of their using to the real earth strain observation in seismic and acoustic frequency bands are discussed.

articleTitle: Mode basis method for spherical tem - transmission lines and antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Mode basis method in spherical coordinate system is considered. Compared to the previous works in this field the method is generalized to take into consideration T-modes in conical lines and more general medium inhomogeneity that contains both radial and angular dependencies. A biconical and alike antennas (bow-tie, blade antenna, V-antenna, TEM-horn, etc.) can be rigorously analyzed with the proposed method.

articleTitle: UWB antenna array development for GPR applications
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Theoretical and experimental studies of the influence of mutual arrangement of wideband tapered slot antennas (TSA) in the array are presented. Major attention is paid to reducing antenna coupling. The modeling was done using a transient solver realized in the CST Microwave Studio software. It was found that a parallel displacement of the antennas in the array when the distance between antenna planes is kept, allows to suppress unwanted lateral coupling that leads in turn to reduction of clutter. The antenna array consisting of the TSA had been fabricated and tested in a test site for the detection of low-contrasted objects like anti-personnel mine.

articleTitle: Directional characteristics of rarefied antennas array with screen
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: It is shown that if the distance between the elements of equidistant arrays of near-omnidirectional radiators is increased from 0.5 to one wavelength, it is possible to increase the directivity D and to reduce the width of the main lobes of the pattern of an antenna array in comparison with the same characteristics of a continuous antenna at a comprehensible level of side lobes. The studied effects can be increased by arranging the radiators above the screen at a height greater than a quarter of the wavelength.

articleTitle: Built-in Performance Monitoring System for Active Phased-array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In active phased array antennas, transmit and receive functions are distributed at the aperture using transmit and receive (T/R) modules. Active phased arrays are typically calibrated in a near-field antenna range at the factory. The performance of active phased array antennas would degrade over time due to changes in the characteristics of active devices and would require recalibration in the field. The conditions and methods required for the active phased-array antenna (APAA) measurements, initial alignment, further automatic diagnostics and performance monitoring are described. Special attention is paid to constructive peculiarities of APAA and measurement restrictions. A numerical model of performance monitoring process has been developed and many test cases examined in an effort to isolate and characterize errors commonly found in the built-in performance-monitoring systems (BPMS). Both simulation and measurement results are presented to demonstrate the utility of the proposed measurement and monitoring techniques. Future research directions in applying BPMS are highlighted.

articleTitle: Turnstile antenna for saddle pattern generation in Leo satellite applications
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In this paper, design of a turnstile antenna in UHF band (465 MHz) is carried out. In this design the initial values for monopole lengths and their distances have been considered lambda / 4 and for antenna mounting angles to be 90 degree respect to ground plane (satellite body). The effects of monopole lengths, distances and mounting angle variations studied by antenna modeling with finite elements method (by HFSSV10). The results show that increasing monopole lengths, achieving sharper saddle shaped pattern and decreasing antenna mounting angles, making smoother radiation pattern. For monopoles distances, variation about 10% around lambda / 4 does not affect the radiation pattern, obviously. In this article, optimum values for aforementioned main parameters obtained by search method. The designed antenna with optimum values parameters fabricated and tested. The results represent a good agreement between simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: The adaptive automat for compensation of reduction in antenna gain in a sample of tropospheric radio communication
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In the paper, the solution of the problem of compensation for the reduction in antenna gain is given, made with help of the automat providing both the adaptive equality of two energy parameters of a sample of tropospheric radio communication (TRC) and its information reliability.

articleTitle: Non-uniform amplitude excitation of elements in an antenna array
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Special law of exciting currents' amplitudes distribution is proposed in the paper. It is shown that tapered antenna array with elements excited in accordance to the proposed law can form the directional pattern that is close to one formed by antenna array with equally spaced elements within a limited angular sector. An algorithm that allows to form any desired equivalent amplitude distribution in the equivalent aperture of tapered antenna array is presented as well.

articleTitle: Forming and radiation of high-power short radio pulses
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: An algorithm of synthesis of energy compressors and radiators of high-power short radio pulses has been developed and implemented for the first time on the level of complete electrodynamic models.

articleTitle: Antenna matching for bandwidth enhancement
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A matching technique which simultaneously fulfills 2 tasks, matching and enhancement of the operation frequency band, is presented in this paper. As an example, matching for a 5-band mobile phone (GSM 850, GSM 900, GSM 1800, GSM 1900 and WCDMA 2100) has been examined. Two very simple inverted-L antennas with input impedances in range of 2 - j10 to 10 + j20 Ohms with two matching circuits are used to provide a 50 Ohm matching for all bands. LowBand: GSM 850 + GSM 900. HighBand: GSM 1800 + GSM 1900 + WCDMA 2100. The target for return loss was selected 3.5 VSWR. The rejection of LowBand at HighBand -and vice versa -is better than 25 dB, so no further diplexing would be needed in the front end. The size of one matching component is 1.6 times1.8 times 1.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The overall antenna efficiency (at 50 Ohm terminal) is 52-60% min at LowBand and 65-70% at HighBand.

articleTitle: Transient radiation from the open end of circular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The transient radiation from the open end of a circular waveguide is considered by simple analytical and direct numerical methods. The radiation of short pulse from the aperture is provided by calculation of special time form of field by means of modal basis method that permits to solve the problem of pulse evolution for positive and negative time with the use of Laplace transform. The radiation of the short pulse is calculated in Kirchhoff approximation and simulated by FDTD method. The frequency characteristics of the radiated field are considered.

articleTitle: A novel coaxial CTS antenna design
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: CTS (Continuous Transverse Stub) antenna radiates electromagnetic wave with its transverse stubs on transmission line, and its pattern in horizon plane is omnidirectional. This paper proposes a novel coaxial CTS structure, in which a monopole is applied in coaxial CTS antenna, instead of a matching load. This method may not only improve the radiation ratio, but also reduce the height of antenna. There are two stubs and a monopole composing an antenna, and the dielectric in stubs is air, which could predigest the manufacture progress. Through the electromagnetic simulation software CST MICROWAVE STUDIO®, properties of the CTS antenna working at 12GHz is obtained by finite integral method. The monopole ending makes the radiation efficiency higher, and keeps the input impedance of CTS antenna. The gain is higher than that of three-class coaxial CTS. For its characteristics, the antenna could be used in retransmission and personal communication system.

articleTitle: A scanning measuring radiometry complex with computer control
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: For the forming of images in radiometry, the multichannel receivers with the matrix or linear feeds of the antenna aperture are used, as well as the scanning-type single-channel radiometers. The simplicity of the antenna system and the absence of the inter-channel effects, at a lesser total cost, is the advantage of the single-channel scanning radiometers. Nevertheless, the scanning radiometers, in this regard, are very critical concerning the exact spatial positioning of the antenna system over the process of scanning. To ensure a high quality of the images, a computer-controlled scanning radiometry complex is developed by the authors; both the mechanical process of scanning and the transform of the output signal into digital form are provided via computer.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic modeling, optimization and on-site verification of electromagnetic fields exposure from high power rf sources
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Human hazard consequent to electromagnetic exposure is identified and controlled by civil and military recommendations and laws. When the exposure impact is due to high average power electromagnetic sources, it is mandatory to approach the siting evaluation and installation together with the human hazard aspect. Main steps are: development of a state-of-the-art electromagnetic model of the sources, embedded on the surrounding structures with details of materials and geometry; development of an optimization procedure aimed to maintain adequate Quality of Service and minimize the exposure; on-site test of the source, aimed to confirm the applied hypothesis and to certify the status of the area. The details of these steps are described, based on innovative modeling and measurement experiences on a large number of new high power multimedia telecommunication systems.

articleTitle: Active noise interference compensation in forward-scattering radar with array
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The paper deals with bistatic forward scattering radar (FSR) with continuous quasi-harmonic probing signal or continuous wave (CW) FSR, briefly. The algorithm of active noise interference adaptive compensation in CW FSR with array antenna is considered. The particular feature of the used array antenna is digital beam forming executed after the amplitude detection in the receiving channels of the array elements.

articleTitle: Extension of diffraction theory heuristic methods feasibilities by use of the method of generalized eikonal
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The method of generalized eikonal (MGE) described in a number of recent publications allows to receive in a fairly simple way considerably rigorous analytical solutions describing processes of diffraction on two-dimensional scatterers of a complex shape. The constructed solution represents an integral representation in a auxiliary area, similar to one that turns out during the process of wedge diffraction problem solving. The general view of such representation is known beforehand, while concrete solutions depend on the shape of corresponding scatterers. This paper presents the basics of MGE, solution for the diffraction by a half-plate with finite thickness. The usefulness of this method in heuristics approaches of the diffraction theory is shown.

articleTitle: Modeling of Horn Array Antennas with Protruding Dielectric Elements
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A 2D problem of E-polarized wave radiation from an infinite array of stepped horns with dielectric elements passing through the horns and protruding above the horn apertures is considered. A hybrid projection method of solution reducing the problem to a system of ordinary differential equations for variable coefficients of the field expansion is proposed. The differential equations are subsequently reduced to linear algebraic equations after applying the one-dimensional method of finite elements. The solution of the algebraic system is used for calculation of the array reflection coefficient and element pattern. Some new numerical results characterizing both the method itself and the capabilities of the horn-dielectric arrays are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Wi-Fi networks user’s terminal phased antenna array
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Wireless local networks of Wi-Fi standard, which are actively used presently, is supposed application nondirectional antennas. For the increase of efficiency of communication lines between user’s terminals and access points it is better to use the directional antennas with the control radiation pattern. The results of theoretical and experimental research of 4 and 8 elements phased antenna array of ranges are inprocess presented 2.4 and 5 GHz of radiation pattern maximum changeable direction. The overall sizes of antennas allow to build them in user’s terminals.

articleTitle: Radiation of electromagnetic field pulses by planar dipole antennas at different modes of excitation
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The results of experimental investigations of time-amplitude dependences of impulse electromagnetic fields in near and far zone of radiators are presented in the given work. There have been considered the dependence of amplitude and pulse waveforms on radiator configuration and modes of antenna excitation: with energy storage directly in the antenna and with energy storage in capacitors of an external generator. The comparison of time-amplitude dependences of the radiated field for the "bow-tie" radiator and a modified "diamond dipole" with different angular dimensions has shown that the "diamond dipole" with angular dimension of 180deg has a maximal pulse amplitude and minimal duration of afterpulse oscillations of the radiated field. It has been shown that for all radiator types been considered, the antenna excitation by a generator with energy storage directly in the radiator permits to increase the amplitude of the radiated pulse field by 5-15 %.

articleTitle: Broadband antenna array for mobile radiocomminication
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The paper presents results of computer simulation and measured characteristics of the broadband antenna array for mobile radiocommunication system. Proposed multiport antenna array work in the octave in L-S frequency band. The inhomogeneous microstrip power divider for excited antenna array is proposed too. Power divider characteristics are presented in this paper. Problem of broadband matching of the antenna array is discussed.

articleTitle: Modeling dipole antenna arrays placed, near to interface between two media
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A modeling technique of antenna arrays made from horizontal wire dipoles located over an interface of two media is developed. It is based on the moment method for wire antennas. The emphasis is placed on evaluating matrix parameters of radiation system and using them for analysis of power characteristics of ground based antenna arrays, especially of their efficiency dependence from the input currents distribution. Numerical analysis results are given for the radiation efficiency of the phased antenna array, located near the ground surface, at beam scanning in the elevation plane.

articleTitle: Frequency selective surfaces with L-shaped apertures
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Scattering of a plane wave by frequency selective surfaces perforated with one or several L-shaped apertures are proposed. Depending on the surfaces layouts they can lead to the transmission or hybrid response. Features and advantages providing by the L-shaped apertures are discussed.

articleTitle: Research and design on ultra-wideband dielectric hemispheric lens loaded quad-ridged horn antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Based on the ultra-wideband ridged horn antenna theory in communication system, a new quad-ridged horn antenna with a lens is described in this paper, which consists of a quad-ridged horn and a dielectric hemispheric lens. By simulation and optimization with CST MWS software which is based on the Finite Integration Technique a dual polarization dielectric lens loaded quad-ridged horn antenna can realize higher gain and ultra-wideband character. The result shows that in ideal state, the dielectric lens can increase the gain of quad-ridged horn antenna with 3 dB and the 15 dB gain is very important in some application. Besides, the volume of the system does not largen much. The simulated return loss S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> of the horn antenna system is better than −10 dB during the operating frequency band from 2 GHz to 18 GHz. Also, for its own structure of the quad-ridged horn antenna, it can realize dual polarization character as describe in this paper. The simulation results and analyses of the ultra-wideband quad-ridged horn antenna are presented.

articleTitle: Stop bandwidth extremums of a periodic iris-loaded circular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The stop bandwidth extremums in the eigenwave mode of a periodic iris-loaded circular waveguide are presented for all of the wave types in the structure; the waveguide dimensions are the arguments. The initial attempt at physical analysis is made via a comparison between the different wave types.

articleTitle: Time and frequency analysis of signals used in pulsed antenna ultra-wideband radiocommunication systems
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The paper presents theoretical time and frequency analysis of signals used in modern ultra-wideband (UWB) systems. This analysis is an important part of proposed complex approach to design of UWB antennas. Three popular pulses are described: Gaussian and Rayleigh pulses and UWB wavelet. Different types of impulse modulation used in UWB systems were described and the results of computer simulation are shown in the paper.

articleTitle: Influence of diffraction effects on radiation of the electric dipoles located inside П-figuration corner reflector
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Based on the uniform geometric diffraction theory method the algorithms and programs for calculation of directive patterns of the orthogonal components of the electric field intensity vector of a dipole with the various orientation, located inside pi-figuration finite size infinitely thin perfectly conducting corner reflector, throughout the observation space in the far zone are developed. The analysis of the patterns and the dependences of the radiation resistance, the directive gains and the back to front ratio on the distance between the dipole and the reflector were carried out at varying the lateral ledges width. Diffraction effects on the ledges considerably improve electrodynamic radiation characteristics of the dipole oriented parallely to them.

articleTitle: The Family of Atomic Functions and Digital Signal Processing in Synthetic Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The report consists of two parts. In the first part, the sampling analysis of weight windows is conducted on the basis of atomic functions (AF) and their application in problems of the classical method of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is considered. The second part contains fundamentals of a modified method of synthetizing the aperture. The modified ambiguity function for different signals is probed. The lacks of the Ambiguity function are detected at a modified method. The paths of elimination of the indicated lacks are offered by introduction of weight processing in a technique of the modified method. The expediency of application of weight windows based on AF in reduced problems is empirically justified.

Author Keywords: modified method of synthesis of the aperture

articleTitle: Research of Radiation Characteristics of Z Antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Results of research of characteristics of radiation log-periodic Z antennas are submitted. The opportunity of formation one of directed radiation is shown. Geometrical parameters for formation of a mode of return radiation are received.

articleTitle: Design & fabrication of turnstile antenna with feed network optimization for Leo satellites
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In this paper design of a turnstile in UHF band (465 MHz) is carried out. Optimum values for its main physical parameters such as monopole lengths, monopoles distance and angles are obtained by using HFSSV10 software. Antenna feed network is designed with microstrip lines to achieve in to the 90 degrees phase difference between adjacent monopoles and small size, simultaneously. Obtained scattering parameters from antenna design are used with microstrip feed network in microwave office software to achieve the desired VSWR characteristic of antenna at 465 MHz. In next step, the line and stub lengths are optimized in order to achieve a return loss better than 20 dB in operation frequency. Variable lumped capacitors are used in designed feed network for frequency fine tuning. The designed antenna and feed network are fabricated and tested. The diagrams represent a very good agreement between simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: A study on methods of microwave wood drying
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Two methods of reduction of microwave power reflection from a wood stack are studied theoretically. The first method consists in choice of such slope angle of the radiating aperture at which a phenomenon of the Brewster takes place. The second method is based on application of the metal grid located between an radiator and a stack. The optimum relations for a choice of a grid cell size and a grid location are obtained.

articleTitle: Analytical and numerical method for solving model problems of slotted cone antenna impulse excitation
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A new analytical numerical method for solving initial boundary problems with conical and wedge geometry is proposed. The method is based on using the Meller-Fock integral transforms and the regularization method. Analytical solutions of the impulse excitation problem for a slotted cone structure are obtained.

articleTitle: The reflectivity investigation of satellite and ground based antennas AT 100-380 GHZ and 80 K
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The satellite and ground based antenna reflectivity investigations have been made. It was revealed that the reflective coverings of some composite carbon fibers antennas have inadmissibly more reflective losses which lead to the essential noise temperature increasing of high sensitive cooled receivers. The significant anisotropy of carbon fibres antenna covering have been found. Unexpected reflectivity behaviour of satellite antenna reflectors at liquid nitrogen temperatures was found.

articleTitle: Experimental study on fan-beam cassegarian antenna fed by a 4-element binomial array
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Present paper describes the development of a fan-beam cassegarian antenna unit being fed by a 4-element binomial array with centre frequency of 2.45 GHz with a 4 set of well matched microstrip dipole units.

articleTitle: Influence of microwave irradiation on the blood of men
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Influence of microwave radiation on immunological indexes of practical healthy people is studied. An index of T-cells immune system is investigated.

articleTitle: Scattering of an E-polarized plane wave by elongated cylinder of arbitrary cross-section
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The rigorous solution for the scattering of an electromagnetic E-polarized plane wave by an infinite solid cylinder of arbitrary cross-section is used to estimate the scattering by a finite elongated cylinder. The rigorous solution for an infinite cylinder is obtained by the method of regularization. This provides a stable and fast converging algorithm, which guarantees the computation of the scattered electromagnetic field with any desired accuracy. The computational algorithm is uniformly valid for studies of electromagnetic scattering in a wide frequency range, when the maximum size of the cylinder cross-section may vary from a fraction of a wavelength to a few hundred wavelengths. The rigorous solution has been implemented for the analysis of scattering by finite elongated cylinders, using well-known approximation techniques. The scattering by cylinders with a super-ellipse cross-section is investigated for a variety of practical cross-sections described by the generalized super-ellipse parametric equation.

articleTitle: Near-field radiation from sectoral horns
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The purpose of the presented work is to investigate the forming of radiation at the plates in the "near-field reactive" regions of rectangular waveguides and sectoral horns. The influence of quadratic phase distortions at the horn aperture on forming the radiation in the near-field region is investigated. The possibility to form the axi-symmetric radiation characteristics of horn radiators in near zone by means of appropriate choice of the value of quadratic phase distortions and horn geometrical sizes is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Enclosed coaxial waveguide antenna array for a ground-penetrating radar
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In this paper the phased array of enclosed coaxial waveguides has been theoretically considered as antenna for ground-penetrating radar. The reflected and transmitted signals were obtained using the inverse Fourier transform. The reflection and transmission coefficients for the elements of array with monochromatic excitation can be founded using the variational principle in single-mode approximation. Some numerical results for array of two enclosed coaxial waveguides with a pulse excitation are presented.

articleTitle: Designing of multifrequency wire antennas with shunts
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The results of research and designing of multifrequency wire antennas with concentrated and distributed reactive loads for mobile terminals are considered. Designing of multifrequency antennas is offered for carrying out in three stages.

articleTitle: Helix antennas for generators of short high-voltage pulses
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Distinctive features of high-voltage systems of generator and radiating antennas, that we developed, are: highest possible working voltage and electric field intensities in dielectric media of generator and antenna, limited from above by electric strength of dielectric media; possibility to connect small-size forming low-impedance output device of generator to antenna ports through fast-acting high-voltage switches; radiating helix antennas for forming low-impedance output device of the generator are long lines which wave impedance is essentially more than inner impedance of forming device. Conic helix antennas, working in the mode of practically axial radiation, connected with their one end (from the broad part) to plane low-voltage shield, and with their another end (from the narrow part), through conductor located on antenna axis, -to high-voltage output of low-voltage forming device of the generator, are, from our point of view, the most suitable for high-voltage generators with low inner impedance. Evaluation has shown that helix antennas are superior to TEM-horns in efficiency of radiation of short pulses, obtained with help of low-ohmic forming devices. Expected level of working pulse voltage on used helix antennas is more than 500 kV.

articleTitle: UWB radiating antenna arrays with strong coupling between the elements
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Various layouts of the UWB radiating antenna array consisting of the large current radiators as antenna array elements are discussed in the paper. Influence of the mutual coupling between the antenna elements for the strong and weak coupling cases is investigated. Obtained dependencies of the radiation efficiency versus the mutual coupling factor and the antenna array layout (the vertical array or the horizontal array) are shown and discussed. It was found out that increase of the coupling between the vertical arrays elements results in increase of the vertical antenna array radiation efficiency and decreases the last one if radiating antenna is horizontal array of the large current radiators.

articleTitle: Extension minimum method for determination of antenna pattern from near-field measurements
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The problem of far-field pattern estimation from near-field data measurements through determination of currents distribution on the aperture plane is considered. Extension minimum method is applied for currents estimation problem, which outperforms standard regularization technique, when there is a priori information about finiteness of unknown support of currents on aperture plane. Fourier transform applied afterwards to determine far-field pattern. Arc-shaped scanning geometry is used for numerical simulation. Results are presented for one-dimensional aperture case.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of the disk modulated impedance antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In given paper the results of development of the mathematical model of the disk modulated impedance antenna are resulted. The model is presented by some class of the branched continual fractions. Such fractions describe themselves electrodynamics characteristics of the modulated impedance structures as functions of parameters of their construction. The results of the numerical and experimental researches of the antenna's electrodynamics characteristics are resulted.

articleTitle: Microwave scattering on atmospheric particles
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The models of microwave scattering on atmospheric particles are presented. Shape, size, material, and other properties of scatterers are taken into account at different wave polarizations. Results are important for remote recognition of hydrometeor types, radar and telecommunications.

articleTitle: Microwave spherical focusing systems
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Microwave focusing systems of spherical shape (constant K-lens, Luneberg lens and spherical reflector antenna) are investigated. The corresponding wave scattering problems are treated as classical boundary value problems for Maxwell's equations. The systems are illuminated by an electromagnetic plane wave (receiving) and by a complex-point huy-gens source producing a Gaussian beam-like radiation (transmitting). In the case of a spherical lens the electromagnetic field has an explicit mie series representation. When investigating the spherical reflector antenna and spherical lens reflectors we employ the rigorous method of regularization. This method provides stable and fast converging computational algorithms, which guarantee any desired accuracy of the computations. The specific computational tools are implemented to advance into the deep quasi-optical region, where electrical size of an aperture D/lambda is specified by thousands. These advances are employed for comprehensive analysis of the giant spherical reflector antennas (up to D/lambda = 10000 ). The performance of low-profile multi-beam antennas based on spherical lenses is examined when the interference between beams is "automatically" incorporated into the general solution. The comparative analysis of the Luneberg lens and Constant-K lens reflectors is performed in a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: The near zone field of crossed impedance vibrators in absorbing medium over the perfect conducting plane
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The investigations of distribution of the near zone electromagnetic fields of the thin crossed impedance vibrators situated in absorbing medium over the infinite perfect conducting plane have been made. The possibility of creation of the radiation field of circular (elliptic) polarization at the expense of a definite value and a type of surface impedance of each of vibrators is shown.

articleTitle: Integrated immersion lens antennas for millimeter and submillimeter wave array detectors
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Two variants of an integrated lens antenna for millimeter and submillimeter-wave array receivers are analyzed. One of the variants consists of a single-chip planar array placed into a focal plane of a large immersion silicon lens. For the second case, we consider an array of multiple integrated lens antennas; each single detector is coupled to its individual immersion lens. We compare two designs of an array of TES (transition edge sensor) detectors coupled into cross-double-slot antennas at 250 GHz [1]. We define limiting parameters of the imaging array antenna configuration using a tolerance analysis, which includes beam degradation criterion for edge pixels due to aberrations in the common optical system.

articleTitle: An antenna ship RLS with a reflector element as a cutting-out from the parabolic cylinder
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: We carried out calculation of the geometrical sizes of the antenna as a cutting-out from the parabolic cylinder, set up on methods of ray optics. The received design formulas are used for numerical modeling on the computer of the shape of the antenna reflector of millimeter band.

Author Keywords: breadth of an antenna directional pattern

articleTitle: Circular polarization broadband antenna feed
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In work results of research of mutual influence of spiral radiators in an array are submitted with the purpose of expansion of a frequency band by the antenna of system and the further improvement of its characteristics.

articleTitle: New absorbing materials for applications in decimeter and millimeter wavelengths ranges
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The results of tests of the several absorbing materials in the millimeter band are presented. It is shown that at frequencies 140 GHz the absorbing-diffusing materials decrease the reflection from the metallic plate by a value of 34 dB for wide angles range. For the equipment of anechoic chambers there were developed the versions of materials with the lowered combustibility and improved operating characteristics, including the material, closed with a case, laminated by polyethylene fiberglass fabric. There were investigated the composite materials on the basis of magnetoamorphous and nano-crystalline alloys of Fe-Si-B type for 300-1500 MHz frequency region. The two-layered material provided to reduction in the reflection by a value of 10.. .22 dB in 400-800 MHz frequency band.

articleTitle: Minimization of phase noise in scaled device coupled mode oscillators
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The performance of the electronic system strongly depends on the speed of devices, and device scaling has driven this momentum towards achieving faster speed and high level of integration. This paper describes the impact of phase noise in scaled SiGe HBTs coupled mode oscillators topology, which has recently emerged as a strong contender for RF and mixed signal applications. The relative contribution of the broadband (thermal and shot noise) and low frequency (1 / f noise) noise sources are examined with respect to the device scaling. A method of minimizing the phase noise with respect to the device scaling is discussed, and demonstrated for planar coupled resonators based VCO. The circuit topology is not limited to these frequencies, and easily amenable for integration in MMIC form.

articleTitle: Scattering fields of chiral layers periodical sequence
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The electromagnetic fields of the chiral layer bounded sequence are investigated. The diffraction problem is solved with using the circuit theory and matrix function methods. The frequency and angle dependencies of the scattering coefficients are given. The boundaries of quasi-passing (quasi-locking) zones are determined from the eigenvalue analysis of the basic element transmission matrix.

articleTitle: Application of wavelet transform to the solution of scattering problems
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In this work the application of wavelets for the increase in the efficiency of the solution of an integral equation, which describes a scattering problem is considered. Examples of fractal wire antennas calculations are used to show the applicability of wavelet basis functions. The precision of the obtained results is estimated.

articleTitle: The analysis and simulation of ellipsoid antenna for millimeter-wave imaging
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Using numerical analysis methods, this paper analyzes the focusing characteristics of the circular aperture ellipsoidal antenna, introduces the basic tenets of initiative and passive millimeter-wave imaging and their respective characteristics. As to the ellipsoid right antenna system for millimeter-wave imaging, this paper analyzes the near-field field-strength and resolution so on. In the end, this paper indicates that ellipsoid antenna used for security checking has special advantages.

articleTitle: Features of the aperture antenna radiation field, stipulated by the influence of turbulent inhomogeneities
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: For the first time, the analysis of the field radiation pattern (RP) of aperture antennas is carried out taking into account the fluctuations of angles of wave arrival. Formulas for the mean RP are arranged in view of the angular deviation of the maximum radiation direction.

articleTitle: Microwave measurement of directories and foweve electronics & their applications
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In the first part of presentation it is planned to present the wide review of all the method of microwave methods of measurements of linear dielectric and non-linear dielectrics as ferroelectrics.

articleTitle: The simulation of effective parameters of composite media with embedded metal-dielectric thin fibers
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The simulation results of effective parameters of composite media with embedded metal-dielectric thin fibers are given in the paper.

articleTitle: Numerical study of 32 element phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The paper presents the numerical study of 32-element phased-array antenna with 16-elements beam units along with 16 elements beam steering units. In the subsequent part deals with the working plan related with the radiating units and phase-shifter.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic modelling of system of two vibrators on transitive compartment accelerating of block «frigate»
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The example 2D modelling by method Rtau-grid directional pattern of system of two vibrators on a transitive compartment accelerating block "Frigate" with cowl is resulted. The directional pattern of the considered system of the vibrators, received in anechoic box on an antenna breadboard model is resulted. Qualitative concurrence of settlement and experimental directional patterns is shown.

articleTitle: Antenna beam scanning via aperture synthesis
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A new concept for scanning antennas design is suggested. The concept is based upon a combination of a single radiating element movement with antenna aperture synthesizing. The radiator movement may be implemented either in direct way or virtually via switching of feeding circuitry of the antenna ID array. The latter may be done either electro-mechanically or electronically. In the paper, the case of electromechanical movement of the radiator is preferably considered. Various realizations of real and virtual movements of the radiator are briefly described. Examples of the concept implementing are presented. Advantages and drawbacks of the concept are discussed.

articleTitle: Back propagation neural network method of solution of normal fat dipole and truncated conical grounded monopole and optimization by genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In order to regularize the software by Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN) two types of dipoles viz. normal fat dipoles as treated in many handbooks and truncated conical dipoles are selected in this paper. The first type is essentially to find out the feasibility of BPNN software to be applied for grounded truncated conical monopole. The second case is a semi-empirical approach that has been developed, where from the optimal dimensions are selected by means of genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: Sensitivity characteristics of different configurations of software gradiometers used in magnetocardiography
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: It is common to use high-order (2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup>) gradiometers in magnetocardiographic measurements to filter out environmental noise. Such gradiometers consist of several coils connected serially with different polarity. Contemporary technology allows using software gradiometers, which measure signal from each coil separately and sums them with required weights at post processing. So there is a possibility to combine the signals from elementary sensors in different configuration by setting different weights. Such different schemes can be used for purposes of background noise filtering and solving the inverse problem. The subject of this study is to compare several summing configuration in terms of sensitivity to the source parameters.

articleTitle: Resonance degenerate plane lattice of magnetodielectric spheres with a hole
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The solution of the problem on electromagnetic waves scattering by a plane lattice of magnetodielectric spheres, in which the lattice degenerate resonance is excited, is considered.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of multi-beam reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The method of physical optics was used for the numerical analysis of the basic characteristics and parameters of a multi-beam reflector antenna with the feed of a linear pyramidal-horn array, excited by the principal TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> mode.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of wire multi-element antenna array
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The numerical modeling of multi-element antenna array is needed for analysis of interactions between antenna array elements. This interaction considerably change impedance and directivity diagram of one radiation element situated in antenna array in comparison with isolated radiation element. More accurate numerical method for analysis wire antenna is integral equation method (IE), but its capability is considerably limited by irradiator wave dimension. The work deals with two methods for sur- mounting this limitation.

articleTitle: A discussion on the properties of electrically small fractal antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The performance properties of several electrically small, self-resonant fractal antennas (ESFA) are compared as a function of their total wire length, geometry, and effective volume. The radiation properties considered include resonant frequency, radiation resistance, and quality factor. It is shown that the resonant properties of these antennas are directly a function of the antenna's effective height and effective volume, which are established by both total fractal length and fractal geometry. To estimate the a-forms, possible algorithms are formulated, permitting the Hausdorff measure to be evaluated through application of fractional derivatives and integrals. It is shown, that these properties of ESFA are practically realized due to use structured artificial conducting fractal material elements.

articleTitle: Diffraction of light wave on bi-dimensionally periodic metallic nanogratings. theoretical study
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The paper suggests a model to address the problem of enhanced optical transmission through doubly periodic metallic nanostructures. The theoretical model combines integral equations method with impedance boundary conditions in rigorous fashion and enables modeling nanostructures with apertures of different shape. Numerical results obtained with the model have been shown to be in a good agreement with experimental ones. A comparison between square and circular aperture array enhanced transmission properties has been carried out as well.

articleTitle: A dual-polarization channels models of digital antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This report deals with a compact matrix record of the reception channels responses for the multicoordinate digital beamforming systems with dual-polarization channels of antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Electrodynamics characteristics of the transversal slot radiator in a rectangular waveguide with a layered dielectric filling
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Physical properties of transversal slot radiators in a rectangular waveguide with a dielectric layer parallel to its broad walls were studied. It has been shown that it is possible to slow down effectively the waveguide wave and to control the level of power radiated and reflected by the slot choosing in a proper way the thickness of the dielectric layer and its permittivity.

articleTitle: Intellectual multisurvey processing of radar information
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Intellectual system algorithms of low-sized air objects detection against radar clutters are offered. These algorithms, based on predicate algebra techniques, provide automation of multisurvey information processing and increase detection efficiency due to accumulation of signal (power) and logic information in analyzed resolution cell and its neighborhood. Thus processing speed (data-rate) is increased and online data processing.

articleTitle: Some potentialities and prospects of the partial scattering operators method
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Partial scattering operators method (PSOM) has been proposed at the millennium conference on antennas and propagation held in Davos in 2000. After that with the aid of this method the explicit analytical solution of the diffraction of the point-source field on a slot problem has been obtained. In this report I would like to outline some problems which has been solved and can be solved with the aid of the PSOM.

articleTitle: To calculation of the signal/noise ratio on an output of the active phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In work the factors determining the basic electric characteristics of an active phased array antenna as the aerial of system are analyzed. The design procedure of the relation signal/noise on its output is set up. Results can be used for optimization both structure of the transmit-receive module, and infrastructure phased array antenna.

articleTitle: Design of spmt switches matched by means of transforming four-poles
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In this paper the method for calculation of single pole multi-throw (SPMT) switches insertion loss and isolation which can be obtained at the assigned type of the switching elements and its connection circuit is offered. The formulas for determination of electrical parameters of elements of transforming four-poles circuits which are necessary to provide the SPMT switch mentioned parameters and input matching of it are resulted The method for compensation of effect of discontinuity of lines branching, which is part of such devices, is also offered.

articleTitle: SAR imaging based upon nonswitchable antenna array and noise signals
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The work is devoted to elaborating a new method for SAR image generating using noise/random signals and nonmoving & non-switching antenna array suggested in Lukin (2006). The main idea of that antenna array consists in the extraction from the total signal of one channel receiver the signals received by a single element of the array. This signals separation is based upon decorrelation properties of noise/random signals. Attractive advantages of the suggested antenna array and the method for SAR imaging consist in no need in either mechanical motion or electronic switching of the antenna array elements, which simplify its design and lower the cost. Analytical evaluations for main performance of such antenna array are given for its various implementations. The related SAR imaging algorithm is described in detail. Some results of computer modeling of SAR imaging using this antenna array are presented. Advantages and constraints of the method and array suggested are discussed.

articleTitle: Localization of the reflecting centers using multifrequency and multiposition antenna scanning
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The problem of processing for multifrequency and multiposition cross-section scanning data has been considered. The method of quasisolution searching with compromise model of interaction of the reflecting centers and antenna has been used. The accuracy properties of the method have been analyzed.

articleTitle: Solid state nonstationary spectrometers SUBTHz and THz frequency ranges for analytical applications
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In the paper we present a new approach to development of a time-domain (pulse Furier-transform) spectroscopy method in subTHz and THz frequency ranges with maximal sensitivity and spectral resolution. In our studies we obtained harmonics up to 2.7 THz with application of multipliers based on quantum superlattice structures. Our spectrometer includes subTHz and THz emission sources based on phase-stabilized Gunn generators and quantum superlattice structures multipliers and mixers (up-converter). This approach ensures narrow instrumental linewidth less than 10 kHz over the operating range of the spectrometer as well as development of software for computer control and data acquisition. In the paper we propose two possible schemes of spectrometers realization. These variants of spectrometer are suitable, in particular, for atmospheric investigations, including detection of water, acetone, NO, CO etc. nonstationary THz spectrometer

articleTitle: On the development of efficient computational algorithm for transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A computational algorithm based on modified mode matching technique in developed for finding the guided modes in a waveguide with a complicated cross sectional structure. Some specific futures of developed algorithm are discussed. On the paper the algorithm is presented by example, namely the eigenmodes problem of ridged waveguide with thick ridge in H-plane and as particular cases of this problem reshaped waveguide and ridged waveguide with thin ridge are also considered.

articleTitle: A study on the modelling of the electromagnetic model base on visual human
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In this paper the research of the effects of electromagnetic radiation on human body are summarized. The statement and method for the analysis in China and abroad has been presented, especially the modeling of human body before the simulation. At last, some suggestions and ideas are made.

articleTitle: Wire curvilinear antennas with impedance elements
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Ways of increase of calculation accuracy the any curvilinear wire antennas with the concentrated impedance elements are considered. It is offered to approximate curvilinear the closed or opened wire antennas by the geometrical curves of the maximum order, modernized and usual Cassiny’s ovals and lemniscate, solving the integral equation a numerical method by means of universal algorithm.

articleTitle: Compact reflector antenna with the monopole sub-reflector
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This paper is devoted to designing and manufacturing the compact wideband reflector antenna with the monopole sub-reflector. Based on the computation modeling and experimental investigations the effect of separate elements of the proposed antenna on the radiation characteristics is studied. The regularities of radiation pattern shape are determined. Finally, the experimental antenna prototype is described, as well as the input antenna characteristics, near-field distributions and radiation pattern are analyzed.

articleTitle: A new broadband UHF antenna with controlled current distribution
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This paper presents results of the computer-aided design of a new broadband monopole UHF antenna with controlled current distribution (BACCD) for different radiocommunication systems. General structure, computer model and construction of the antenna BACCD are proposed. Optimal broadband matching of the antenna is fulfilled in the work. A method of computer electromagnetic simulation of the whole antenna is described. Frequency characteristics, electromagnetic radiation, near electromagnetic field and current distributions along the antenna BACCD for wide frequency band are calculated in the work.

articleTitle: The short pulse intensification in thin film
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This paper, being a continuation of previous author's works [1-3], is devoted to the investigations of the intensification of short pulse signals in active and ferroelectric films.

articleTitle: The experimental investigation of focusing systems based on microstrip reflectarrays
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Focusing microwave systems design is considered. All researching antennas are manufactured as microstrip reflectarrays. Results numerical and experimental researches are given.

articleTitle: Ultra wideband horn antenna excitation by a crack
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The paper presents the way of ultra wideband horn antenna excitation by a crack, describes designed coaxial-to-waveguide transition apparatus and the pre-production model of ultra wideband horn antenna. The final equation for waveguide input reflectivity is also described. The numerical computation and ultra wideband horn antenna experimental researches results are brought over.

articleTitle: Adaptive techniques of the wavefield formation in random-inhomogeneous multimode propagation channels by the use of large arrays
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: We address the source array synthesis problem in a random propagation channel under the different optimization criteria specified for the remote receiving array, namely, the criteria of (i) the output SNR and (ii) the array gain. For the first step, we discuss the optimal schemes for the source excitation and array beamforming by using a general technique of the eigenvalue-eigenvector expansion associated with the normal-mode model of long-range signal propagation in a channel. Then, we develop an adaptive approach to the source array synthesis which is shown to be an iterative correction of the sources excitation coefficients depending on the signal coherence, the receiving array arrangement in a channel, and also on the modal spectrum of the ambient noise interference. Computer simulation is performed for the vertical source and receiving arrays in random-inhomogeneous environments typical for sound propagation in shallow-water channels from the Barents Sea. The results exhibit distinctly a rather high efficiency of the adaptive synthesis algorithms for various sets of the source and environmental parameters including the signal frequency, distance, vertical locations of the sources and receivers.

articleTitle: Mathematical simulation of near radiation fields for reflector-type antenna with sharp nose radom (two-dimensional problem)
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Analysis of the two-dimensional simulation results of the near radiation and scattering fields of aircraft reflector-type antenna with sharp nose ogive radome are presented. The method is based on solving of the volume integral equations relatively a full field in a radome layer and integral or integro-differential equations relatively a current density on reflectors. After determination of the current density on screens, which simulated reflectors, and the field in a radome layer, the estimation of the field nearby antenna system (under and outside radome) reduce to the quadrature calculations, used integral representations of the fields.

articleTitle: Electrodynamics of regular composite medium with grates of contrast material plates
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The electromagnetic fields of the bounded sequence of the same four-layer heterogeneities are investigated. The heterogeneity is formed by different homogeneous isotropic layers and thick periodical grates of rectangular cross-section infinite plates are made from contrast (silver, silica) materials. The frequency region where silver have both negative and positive permittivity is examined. The grates are considered as homogeneous anisotropic layers with permittivity and permeability effective tensors. The diffraction problem is solved with using the circuit theory and matrix functions methods.

articleTitle: Resolvent operator of maxwell equations for 6-dimentional field vector
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: To consider problems with parameters that change in time it needs to solve the time domain Maxwell's equations. If a medium is inhomogeneous than a problem becomes the initial and boundary value one. To solve such a problem it is convenient to transform the differential equations into integral equation, which contain initial and boundary conditions. This transformation can be done by virtue of the Green's function for the Maxwell equations. The advantages of the Maxwell equation Green's function over the Helmholtz and wave equation Green's functions are that it is a single compact expression governing radiation from any source. It is needed for a description of transient electromagnetic phenomena because such phenomena are characterized as a rule by 6D vector combining electric and magnetic fields. It is especially important for time-varying medium when constitutive laws connect these fields.

articleTitle: Interaction of director antennas in the near-field region
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The interaction between the director antennas, located in the near-field region or incorporated into the equidistant antenna array, or forming an arbitrary group, is analyzed by the integral equations method. In the second case as above the director antennas may have different geometry and, hence, may differ in terms of their medium frequency in the operation range.

articleTitle: VLBI-observation of ‘Huygens’ probe
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: JIVE -Joint Institute for Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) in Europe -has managed under ESA contract the VLBI data acquisition of a stabile carrier-signal from Huygens' probe during landing on Titan in January 2004, using ~17 radio telescopes. Evaluation and investigation of the data is included in the same ESA contract. The scenario was described in a previous ICATT Conference (van 't Klooster, 2005). This presentation provides some published information of Huygens descent-trajectory as derived by JIVE. VLBI can be used for special radio-physical investigations, accurate Doppler information is a by-product. VLBI is applied now and in space-missions to come: probes, landers or spacecrafts for navigational, scientific or even telemetry tasks.

articleTitle: To numerical solution of problem on mean-square approximation of real nonnegative finite function with respect to two variables by module of double fourier transformation
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A nonlinear problem on mean-square approximation of a real finite nonnegative continuous function with respect to two variables by the module of double Fourier integral dependent on two parameters is investigated. Finding the optimum solutions (prototypes of Fourier integral) is reduced to investigation and numerical solution of Hammerstein type nonlinear two-dimensional integral equation. Algorithms for numerical finding the lines of branching and branching-off solutions to this equation are constructed and justified. Numerical examples are given.

articleTitle: The influence of fluctuations of electromagnetic wave angles of arrival on the maximum radiation direction of aperture antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Formulas for assessment of the influence of the wave angles of arrivel fluctuations on the aperture antenna radiation maximum direction are obtained. A model of slow and fast fluctuations of angles of arrival is proposed, which enables one to separate the influence of the atmospheric turbulence of large and small scales.

Author Keywords: fluctuations of angles of wave arrival

articleTitle: Designing adaptive interferometer for landing traffic control systems in the millimeter-wave band
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The results of theoretical and experimental researches of the adaptive triangular based on Casigren millimeter-wave band antennas for the integration of tasks of Air Traffic and weather Surveillance control systems as well as the optocontrolled antennas for wideband radiolocation systems have been presented.
