articleTitle: Design and simulation of novel broadband antenna for mobile telecommunication
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A novel broadband omnidirectional antenna is presented in this paper. The an tenna is proposed for operating at mobile telephone bands. To achieve simple struc ture, the proposed antenna is composed of three monopoles in a plane. The impedance matching and bandwidth for the presented antenna are mainly affected by length and separation of the three monopoles. The theory of basic three monopoles antenna is discussed and simulated. By properly choosing the adequate dimension and adjusting the coupling distance, impedance bandwidth of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> ≪ −10 dB is about 640 MHz, and relative bandwidth is greater than 60 %. The antenna can get omnidi rectional radiation pattern in the whole frequency band. And the main lobe 3 dB width is from 61° to 72.6° in the low frequency without side lobe. The highest gain is stable 4.7 dB. The theory analysis and simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: The simulation research of an S-band low-sidelobe antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: An S-band low-sidelobe antenna is designed and proposed which fosters the character of small size and simple structure with wide bandwidth in this paper. The antenna to be discussed takes the advantage of short - focus paraboloidal reflector with round chip and is fed with half-wave dipole. Adjusting the amplitude-phase distribution of aperture field of the antenna, the demand for low-sidelobe and high gain is satisfied through a wide frequency range. The antenna contributes to the portable device for its short vertical length. Simulated on CST MICROWAVE Studio®, E-plane and H-plane directional diagram results illustrate that the antenna satisfies following character through a wide frequency range: the maximum sidelobe ≤ −20 dB, the gain ≥ 20 dBi, the half-power beam width (HPBW) ≤ 20°. Besides, within the frequency range of the central frequency ± 50 MHz the antenna shows ultra-low sidelobe and satisfies its maximum side lobe ≤−30 dB. At the same time, the collision between low-sidelobe and beam width is solved successfully.

articleTitle: Wave radiation of electrically long axial slot cut into the circular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The scattering problem of electrically long axial slot cut into side surface of the circular waveguide has been considered. Expressions of external self-admittance and transfer conductance were derived. The possibility of creation of a field distribution on the slot forms radiation pattern with low side lobes was shown.

articleTitle: The bounded periodical microstrip-slot structure as a radiating model
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The radiating properties of microstrip-slot structure are examining in connection with problems of high-technological multifunctional elements and radiating systems designing. The special emphasis attends to the investigation of characteristics which depend on the peculiarities of construction. The mathematical simulation data allow to predict the possibility of the functional elements designing with high level of parameters. This pattern contains all the styles that should be used in the paper. The detailed instructions are given below.

articleTitle: A potential of the bistatic SAR for aviation and space deployment
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: It is developed a research of the spatial resolution of the bistatic SAR and determined their potential values by means of spatial frequency method at this article. During solution it is given comparative description for resolution and ambiguity function shape of the monostatic and bistatic SAR. Special attention is attended to research the phase functions which produce the fundamental influence to the spatial response selection. The transmitter and receiver motion tracks of the bistatic SAR which providing the potential values of resolution are determined. The dependences of the spatial resolution from elevation angle of the bistatic system platforms under target are presented.

articleTitle: Asymptotic wave-like modeling of dielectric lenses
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: We propose asymptotic wave-like approximations for the accurate modeling of dielectric lenses used in quasi-optical systems of millimeter, submillimeter, and infrared wave applications. For the comparison, we obtain an exact full-wave solution of two-dimensional focusing lens problem and use it as a benchmark for testing and validation of asymptotic models being proposed.

articleTitle: System spectral analysis of the signals
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The new complex signal analysis method called as system spectral analysis and based on the simultaneous application of the set of linear and non-linear integral transforms is proposed. The abilities of the system spectral analysis at the sample of investigation of the unique natural phenomenon well known as the rogue wave are shown.

articleTitle: On Boundary Conditions on the Curvilinear Metallic Surface
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The impedance cylindrical surface with a discrete change of the curvature radius is considered. It is shown, that the discrete curvature change leads to the discrete change of the charge surface density, normal component of an electric field intensity and phase velocity of a current wave. The boundary conditions for the surface current density, electric field intensity components and phase velocity in the place of discrete curvature change are formulated.

articleTitle: The method for wire radiators analysis in infinite planar phased array
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The method of calculation of wire radiators characteristics in the infinite planar phased array with an oblique-angled grid is developed. Each radiator can consist of a set of arbitrarily oriented in space linear wire pieces, including branches, loops, etc. The moment method is applied, and piecewise sine functions are used as basic and weight ones. The closed analytical expressions as double spectral series are received for elements of the mutual impedances matrix. Comparison with results of other authors carried out.

articleTitle: Electric characteristics of a skin layer of a plasma jet generated as a result of the blank cartridge explosion in a free space
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Complex impedance of an electrically excited skin of the radiating plasma jet generated using an explosive method in free space is estimated for the main stage of the jet existence. The analytical expressions describing the frequency dependence of the complex impedance of a skin layer of the plasma jet have been obtained. The measured characteristics of the plasma are used to calculate the resistance and reactance. The presented numerical results allow one to estimate a radiation efficiency of explosive plasma antennas.

articleTitle: Influence of thickness of perfectly conducting plate on its scattering characteristics
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Scattering characteristics of perfectly conducting rectangular flat plate are analyzed for frequency region near resonance. The finite-difference time-domain method is used in simple and efficient form. Scattering diagram and radar cross-section are examined. The method is tested by integral equation method first and foremost.

articleTitle: Multi-element wire antenna array scattering characteristics numerical modeling
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The new method of antenna scattering diagram and radar cross section calculation for multi-element wire antenna array is present in the work. The new method is combination of thin wire integral equation method and complex object RCS calculation method.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field of dipole antenna in multilayered medium with losses
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In the paper a numerical investigation of near-field of dipole antenna in multilayered structure is carried out. Electromagnetic field distribution and wave decay rate in multilayered medium is investigated for different medium types. A contribution of surface waves with comparison of contribution of body waves in antenna’s field is estimated. Asymptotic expression of radiation pattern (RP) in multilayered medium of dipole antenna is obtained. A case of medium containing a layer with continuous changing of parameters is also considered.

articleTitle: Adaptive array of base station of mobile communication
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The adaptive antenna's system is discussed. The one of three sectors is taken into account. The antenna's pattern has three main lobes. The mutual placing of these lobes determines the signal strength from different direction. The array consists of three elements. The elements are turned each from another on certain angle. The binary law of phase discretes is considered.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of monopulse double-reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The numerical simulation of a monopulse double-reflector Cassegrain antenna has been performed by the method of physical optics. The comparative analysis of feed designs was made for two feed alternatives: a four-mode feed with such modes as TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>,TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf>,TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>,TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, and a four-horn feed with TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode.

articleTitle: Comparison of absorbing boundary conditions for numerical analysis of periodic structures
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Periodic structures like gratings or frequency selective surfaces are widely met in antenna design and applications. Some problems require calculating reflectivity in a wide frequency band. Time domain methods like FDTD are beneficial in such problems since they provide the whole spectrum in a single simulation. A periodic structure is modeled as a Floquet waveguide. In FDTD the simulation region needs to be bound with absorbing boundary condition that imitates a semi-infinite waveguide. We tested several such conditions, which are widely used, and reveal that none of these performs well near cutoff frequencies. The problem is demonstrated on a simple illustrative diffraction problem. Some possible ways of improving ABC to overcome the difficulty are discussed.

articleTitle: Research of inphase arrays from rectangular microstrip antenna of microwave frequency
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: It is developed specified resonator model of single rectangular microstrip antenna (RMA). Matchings design values of resonance frequencies, input impedance of RMA on thick and thin substrates are carried out ( ε ≤ 7 ) with the experimental data available in the literature, confirmed pinpoint accuracy of a used model suffices. With its help the optimal adjustment of numerical models of single RMA and lattices from them are retrieved in the program AWR Microwave Office. Designs of 32-element inphase lattices of RMA with vertical and horizontal polarization with a center frequency of 7.8 GHz on FLAN-3.8 substrate of width 2 mm are developed. Basic performances and the parameters of arrays confirmed with results of experimental researches are calculated.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic pulse diffraction on finite array of 2-D metal cylinders
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The solution of diffraction problem of electromagnetic pulse on finite array of 2-D metal cylinders is done by the method of separation of variables. Two methods are used. First the diffraction problem is solved in frequency domain and with following Fourier transformation the scattered impulse is found out. Second the boundary problem is solved directly in time domain.

articleTitle: Antennas for near-field microwave passive and active sounding
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The formation of the signal measured by electrically small plane antennas in the passive (radiometry) and active (insertion impedance) modes of the subsurface near-field sounding (profiling or tomography) of temperature or permittivity in a dielectric half-space is considered.

articleTitle: Method of analysis of antennas and transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Modeling propagation of electromagnetic waves is present. Differential equations for analysis propagation in transmission line are considered. The building of general algorithm of solving the diffraction problem on waveguide antenna is carried out.

articleTitle: Transient spherical wave front steadying in the near zone of an antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Some concepts of transformation of a transient wave front in the near zone of an antenna into a spherical one in the far zone are considered. The characteristics of an antenna relevant to the wave front like amplitude decay centre, time delay centre and prompt impedance that can be useful in modeling short range radar are discussed.

articleTitle: The Amplitude and Power Criterion in the Synthesis Problems for Waveguide Antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The synthesis problem of the waveguide array according to the prescribed amplitude and power radiation pattern is considered. The mutual coupling of the separate elements of array is taken into account in the process of solution of a direct problem (analysts problem). Variational statement of the synthesis problem is used. The functionals representing a mean-square deviation of the prescribed and received radiation patterns are minimized. The corresponding nonlinear equations are reduced; and the modeling results are shown.

articleTitle: Combined acousto-electromagnetic antennas for radioacoustic sounding of the atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: History of the development of combined acousto-electromagnetic antennas for the atmosphere radioacoustic sounding equipment is briefly considered. Advantages and shortages of combined reflector antennas and combined PAAs are pointed out. The modulation effect of sounding electromagnetic radiation at the sound frequency, which is inherent in the combined antennas, is analyzed. Particular attention is given to the statistical aspects of acoustic PAA operation - to the influence of randomness in the sources distribution in antennas on their radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Sidelobe reduction of two-dimensional waveguide-slot antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The Galerkin's method is applied to the problem of electromagnetic wave radiation by two-dimensional waveguide-slot antenna arrays. The thickness of waveguide walls and interaction between slots were taken into account in numerical calculations.

articleTitle: Complex frequencies of the rectangular resonator with the arbitrary number of the dielectric hetrogeneities
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The calculation of a rectangular resonator with a complex dielectric loading is solved by the method of integral equations of microscopic electrodynamics. The carried out numerical analysis enabled to calculate resonance frequencies and amplitudes of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m0n</sub> fluctuations types depending on dielectric cylinder and dielectric parallelepiped heterogeneities placement in a resonator and its dielectric permittivity.

articleTitle: Planar antenna-coupled detector for matrix systems of millimeter wave imaging
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Planar detector as a microstrip slot antenna loaded directly by a low barrier Schottky diode was under consideration. Modified slot antenna with high directivity, radiation resistance ∼ 800 Ω and good matching with detector diodes at resonance frequency 94 GHz was developed. The main characteristics of planar detectors were measured. It was demonstrated that the maximum of rf-to-dc voltage sensitivity γ ≫ 10000 V/W. Frequency band of the detector was about 8 GHz (at − 3 dB level). The best value of the noise equivalent power NEP ≈ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−12</sup> W Hz <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2</sup> was predicted. Interaction effects in a row of close located planar antennas were investigated. Reduction of interaction by mounting additional shielding pins on a screen was studied. The possibility of the compact arrangement of planar detectors with the period of 3 / 2λ was shown.

articleTitle: Radiation, scattering and receiving of pulse signals for subsurface object identification
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In many papers there are approaches for solving subsurface sensing and identification of subsurface objects based on FDTD methods with original methodic of identification [1,2]. There are not efficient for complex objects and lengthy object (its geometrical size is larger than pulse longitude). In this paper a numerical model for calculating far field scattered by complex objects is described. An evaluation is based on analytical evaluations. The results for some testing objects are represented.

articleTitle: The simulation research of a novel uwb triangle monopole antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Based on that triangle monopole antenna has wide frequency band, this paper proposes a novel composite triangle monopole antenna, which is composed of three similar triangle metal plates. Through the electromagnetic simulation software CST Microwave Studioreg, we obtain its characteristics under the condition that its ground-plate is infinite perfect conductor. The simulation results show that the composite triangle monopole antenna not only has wide impedance frequency band, but also takes up smaller space comparing with triangle rnonopole antenna. On the above foundation, we construct composite triangle dipole antenna with two symmetrical composite triangle monopoles without ground-plate and simulate its impedance characteristic, the simulation results further prove that the composite triangle dipoles antenna has stable input impedance between 0.15 GHz and 2.0 GHz (resistance = 150 Omega, reactance = 0 Omega) and has wide frequency band.

articleTitle: KA-Band, P-I-N switchable antenna array system
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: An original electrically switchable, Ka-band antenna array system has been recently developed, produced, and tested. The system consists of four identical sections, which are connected to radar transmitter/receiver by means of a high-power, multipole P-i-N switch. The introduced P-i-N switch enables for a fast electrical scanning of the antenna beam what essentially extends possible areas of the antenna system application. The antenna system is used in a helicopter collision avoidance, surveillance, and weather radar. This paper describes design features of the antenna system, its main characteristics, results of its testing, and the antenna integration in the radar.

articleTitle: H10 wave diffraction in a rectangular waveguide by a narrow walls impedance jump
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In the present paper by the method of projection matching a solution has been obtained for problems of the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> basic wave diffraction at the joint of a regular and non-regular waveguides. At the decision of problem for a waveguide with impedance walls was obtained dispersion equation in relation to a transverse wave values watch allowed writing down the field in non-regular part. As a result of numeral solution, the quantities of transverse wave values and propagation constants of non-regular waveguide are obtained, which at complex impedance are also complex. The system solution of algebraic equations allowed to calculate the coefficients of reflection and passage, and to set their features at the change of value and reactivity of walls impedance.

articleTitle: The evolution of nonmonochromatic mode fields in a waveguide with space dispersive medium
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: We consider a cylindrical waveguide with layered space dispersive medium: there are no free source and charges. The space dispersion is taken in the constitutive equations as a dependence of the electric induction on the electric field and its space derivatives. Electromagnetic fields are; represented as series of nonmonochromatic mode E -and H -fields. In studying the solvability of evolutionary waveguide equations, we obtain a partial differential equation of Sobolev type. We investigate this equation and develop a new numerical method.

articleTitle: Digital analysis of the non-linear ultrawideband processes
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The continuous wavelet transform, the analytical wavelet transform, the digital wavelet transform and the Wigner transform are proposed to apply for the digital analysis of the non-linear ultrawideband processes. The advantages and the disadvantages of each transform being significant during that application are discussed. As the convincing example, the results of the analysis of the Earth's magnetic field disturbances caused by the rocket "proton" launch taken place 12 February 2000 at cosmodrome Baikonur (Kazakhstan) are considered.

articleTitle: Radiation of planar stripline ultra-wideband antenna for WPAN systems
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The paper presents results of design and computer simulation of planar monopole pulse ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna for WPAN applications. A complex approach to design of UWB antennas was used. Problem of radiation of UWB signals by the antenna was discussed. Electric fields radiated by the antenna for chosen directions were calculated and shown.

articleTitle: Microwave parametric reflectometer
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Parametric calibrated reflectometer with simple implementation is proposed. Based on its mathematical model the systems of measurement and calibration equations are formed and their explicit solutions are taken. These solutions are led to the calculation of the imaginary parts of the unknowns. Moreover conditions of true value choice are determined. The results of experimental investigations of parametric reflectometer implemented in microstrip are also presented.

articleTitle: Noise reduction techniques for configurable RF signal source
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The noise cancellation and noise minimization techniques described in this work can satisfy the need of the present demand for low cost, low noise, low power consumption, compact, configurable RF oscillators/VCOs, and also easily amenable for integration in integrated circuit (IC) technology.

articleTitle: Wide angle scanning spherical reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Scanning limits of antenna beam for telecommunication systems are determined. The moment method was used to define the distribution of current to get the pattern in near field zone for spiral radiator of spherical antenna. The hybrid spiral radiator with optimized geometry is presented.

articleTitle: High-Potential Impulse Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Features and results of study of several variants of impulse antennas intended to optimize design of a feeder and irradiating elements, choose a high-voltage dielectric, and provide an antenna operation in condition of polygon tests are considered. An ultra-short pulse radiator with electrodynamic potential W = 1.2 MV based on impulse reflector antenna (IRA) is described.

articleTitle: Wideband irregular-shaped fractal antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This paper proposes an algorithm of generating fully reproducible irregular fractal structures for antenna design. Three types of pseudorandom fractal clusters are introduced. The multi-frequency behavior of the irregular-shaped fractal antennas is studied by means of numerical analysis. The antenna behavior is studied under feeder displacement. As shown by numerical results feeder displacements allow one to control the spatial-frequency antenna characteristics.

articleTitle: Electrophysical properties of nematic liquid crystals under stationary and microwave electric and magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 2007 6th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The nematic liquid crystals in devices with non-linear characteristics, studies were carried out for their electrophysical properties under stationary and microwave electric and magnetic fields. An essential point of our study is the use of two substantially different types of LC (with Deltaepsiv values of opposite signs) in parallel sets of experiments. This allowed us to account, at a qualitative level, for effects of LC orientation and texture upon bulk electric properties.
